signature: SUBROUTINE DGGRQF( M, P, N, A, LDA, TAUA, B, LDB, TAUB, WORK,

params.name: M
params.reference: The number of rows of the matrix A. $M \ge 0$.

params.name: P
params.reference: The number of rows of the matrix B. $P \ge 0$.

params.name: N
params.reference: The number of columns of the matrices A and B. $N \ge 0$.

params.name: A
params.reference: On entry, the M-by-N matrix A. On exit, if $M \le N$, the upper triangle of the subarray `A(1:M,N-M+1:N)` contains the M-by-M upper triangular matrix R; if $M > N$, the elements on and above the (M-N)-th subdiagonal contain the M-by-N upper trapezoidal matrix R; the remaining elements, with the array `TAUA`, represent the orthogonal matrix Q as a product of elementary reflectors (see Further Details).

params.name: lda
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array A. $\mathrm{LDA} \ge \max (1,M)$.

params.name: TAUA
params.reference: The scalar factors of the elementary reflectors which represent the orthogonal matrix Q (see Further Details).

params.name: B
params.reference: On entry, the P-by-N matrix B. On exit, the elements on and above the diagonal of the array contain the min(P,N)-by-N upper trapezoidal matrix T (T is upper triangular if $P \ge N$); the elements below the diagonal, with the array `TAUB`, represent the orthogonal matrix Z as a product of elementary reflectors (see Further Details).

params.name: ldb
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array B. $\mathrm{LDB} \ge \max (1,P)$.

params.name: TAUB
params.reference: The scalar factors of the elementary reflectors which represent the orthogonal matrix Z (see Further Details).

params.name: WORK

minLength.js: max( max( max( 1, M ), P ), N )

params.reference: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

params.name: lwork
params.reference:
The dimension of the array `WORK`. $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge \max (1,N,M,P)$. For optimum performance $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge \max (N,M,P) \, \max (\mathrm{NB1},\mathrm{NB2},\mathrm{NB3})$, where NB1 is the optimal blocksize for the RQ factorization of an M-by-N matrix, NB2 is the optimal blocksize for the QR factorization of a P-by-N matrix, and NB3 is the optimal blocksize for a call of DORMRQ.

If `LWORK = -1`, then a workspace query is assumed; the routine only calculates the optimal size of the `WORK` array, returns this value as the first entry of the `WORK` array, and no error message related to `LWORK` is issued by XERBLA.

params.name: info
params.reference:
-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if $\mathrm{INF0}= -i$, the i-th argument had an illegal value.
